summary: Full-stack cloud runtimes where coding agents can verify PRs.
editor_note: A coding agent is only as useful as the environment it can test. Niteshift puts setup and services in committed .niteshift files, runs a browser against previews, and sends screenshots or demos to PRs. Unlike a local worktree, the runtime can be shared without sharing a laptop. Ambrook's case shows engineers splitting a large migration into reviewable tasks; credentials, test coverage, and merge decisions still need human ownership.

sources.label: Niteshift committed configuration and secret scopes
Niteshift browser verification and PR artifacts
Ambrook component migration workflow, company-published case

product_evidence.claim: Niteshift's setup agent opens a PR with committed .niteshift configuration for setup, resume, and services. Other tasks use the new configuration after merge; secrets are stored separately with setup and agent scopes.

The browser docs describe a persistent Chromium against the app preview; /browser checks flows, /screenshots adds images to the PR description, and /demo records a walkthrough. Instructions can require these checks.

With Neon connected, each task receives a Postgres branch from a selected parent. Branches persist through resume but may be deleted at archival or expiry; this isolation is a configured integration, not an automatic copy of every database.

The pricing page bills 0.1 credits per active agent minute, with no idle-sandbox charge. Individual is $50/month and Team $250/month in matching credits; model tokens come from the user's API key or subscription.

The Ambrook case describes splitting a Material UI-to-BaseUI migration into a component graph, adding Storybook and visual tests, then using Claude Code and Codex tasks. It reports 58 tasks and 29 merged PRs for that project.
The homepage lists Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi and supports starting work from GitHub comments, Slack mentions, and assigned Linear issues.

market_context.primary_user: Engineering and platform leads configuring shared agent runtimes, plus developers and designers working through repository-backed tasks and pull requests.
market_context.category: Managed full-stack runtimes for coding agents
market_context.differentiation: It combines versioned environment configuration, app services, authenticated previews, and browser-to-PR artifacts while allowing different coding agents in the same stack.
market_context.why_now: The committed configuration docs and Ambrook migration case show how teams can turn isolated agent sessions into repeatable, reviewable development work.

risks.claim: Teams still need test credentials, representative data, and review rules; a browser artifact does not prove correctness. Actual isolation and permissions were not tested in a connected repository.
risks.basis: VentureDex assessment of configuration/browser docs and Ambrook's iterative test setup; public documentation review, not a hands-on trial.

risks.claim: Long parallel runs consume active-time credits and separately supplied model tokens. Database branch expiry can also change task state, so cost and retention need testing against the team's workload.
risks.basis: VentureDex assessment of current pricing and Neon branch lifecycle docs; no billing account or long-running task benchmark reviewed.
